summary: DNSSEC / EDNS0 truncation with TCP-53 egress blocked causing intermittent model-artifact fetch failures
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures retrieving model artifacts and package metadata from S3/CDN from their Private deployment. Error pattern indicates DNS resolution failures for large responses when DNSSEC is enabled and DNS responses are truncated (TC=1). The customer's egress path blocks TCP/53, so DNS cannot fall back to TCP for large/truncated responses. Impact: model pulls fail intermittently, causing cold-start errors and deployment rollbacks in the serving runtime.

Observed behavior: runtime logs show repeated RESOLVE_FAILED errors for asset.hosting.cdn and subsequent model-pull retries that eventually time out. Local dig shows DNS responses with EDNS0 and DO flag set, length > 512 bytes and TC=1. Attempts to open TCP/53 for fallback are blocked by corporate firewall.

Expected behavior: either DNS responses over UDP fit within path MTU (EDNS0 supported) or DNS TCP fallback is allowed so DNSSEC-signed responses can be retrieved and validated. The serving runtime should be able to fetch artifacts reliably without manual intervention from the customer network team.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Private package in customer VPC with default resolver pointing to corporate DNS forwarder.
2) Ensure corporate firewall blocks outbound TCP port 53 and blocks fragmented UDP packets larger than 512 bytes.
3) Enable DNSSEC signing on the authoritative CDN zone used for model artifacts (or use an existing DNSSEC-signed zone).
4) Trigger a model pull for a new model version that references multiple CNAMEs and RRSIG records (this causes large DNS responses).
5) Observe runtime failing to resolve hostnames and model pull eventually timing out with repeated retries.
logs: [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:22:08Z model-puller: resolve('asset.hosting.cdn') -> RESOLVE_FAILED: truncated UDP response, tcp fallback attempted
[net-debug] tcpdump: captured UDP DNS response length 1382, flags: DO, TC=1, EDNS0 present
[net-debug] dig +dnssec asset.hosting.cdn @10.10.10.5 -> status: FORMERR; TC=1; attempted TCP connection to 10.10.10.5:53 -> connection refused
[dns-cache] 2026-03-10T11:22:20Z resolver: validation failed: DNSSEC validation could not be completed due to missing response over TCP-53
investigation_notes: Customer-provided packet captures show large DNS responses being truncated (TC=1). The corp NGFW drops fragmented UDP payloads and denies outbound TCP 53 per egress policy.

Redwood runtime attempts TCP fallback on truncated UDP responses. Because TCP/53 is blocked, the resolver never receives the full DNSSEC-signed RRset and validation fails. This manifests as repeated model pull retries and eventual fetch timeouts.
SRE replicated in lab by configuring a forwarder to respond with EDNS0 large responses and then blocking TCP/53 on the outbound interface; observed identical failures and runtime error traces.
Related PR https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/876 contains telemetry improvements to surface DNS truncation and fallback metrics in console. Linking for visibility.
comments:
2026-03-10 12:05 - Marco Reyes (Support): Thanks for the packet capture — confirmed TC=1 and TCP connect resets from your firewall. Short-term workaround: configure your DNS forwarder to perform TCP transport to upstream resolvers and return a truncated-safe UDP response, or allow outbound TCP/53 from the resolver host.

As a mitigation we can also temporarily disable strict DNSSEC validation in the private control plane (not recommended long-term).

2026-03-11 09:30 - BrightNova NetOps (customer): We have a corporate policy that blocks TCP/53 egress from host subnets. We'll discuss allowing TCP/53 from only the cluster's resolver IPs. Meanwhile can Redwood disable DNSSEC validation?

2026-03-11 11:02 - Marco Reyes (Support): We can provide a temporary toggle on the control plane to relax DNSSEC enforcement for artifact pulls for this deployment. This is a last-resort workaround; recommended permanent fix is to allow TCP/53 egress from your forwarder or enable EDNS0/fragmentation passthrough on the NGFW.

2026-03-12 15:40 - SRE (Eve Chen): Lab validation: enabling TCP/53 egress from resolver host eliminated RESOLVE_FAILED. Also validated that configuring forwarder to always do TCP to upstream resolvers (and return A/AAAA answers over UDP within 512 bytes) also succeeds.
resolution: Investigating long-term safeguards and customer guidance. Current recommended fix: allow outbound TCP/53 from the customer's DNS forwarder or enable EDNS0/fragmentation pass-through on the NGFW. We provided a temporary control-plane toggle to relax DNSSEC enforcement for artifact fetches for this deployment while customer evaluates firewall change. Scheduled follow-up to audit audit logging and update runbook.
workaround: 1) Permit outbound TCP/53 from the resolver host(s) to public DNS or Redwood endpoints; OR 2) Configure your DNS forwarder to fetch records over TCP from upstream and synthesize small UDP replies to clients; OR 3) (temporary) Request Redwood to enable DNSSEC-validation-relax toggle on your private control plane until firewall rule change is implemented.
next_steps: SRE to add console telemetry to flag repeated DNS truncation incidents per deployment (linked PR).
Customer to open change request with NetOps to allow TCP/53 from resolver IPs or adjust NGFW fragmentation rules.
Support to schedule a 1:1 walkthrough with BrightNova NetOps and SRE to verify post-change behavior and remove the temporary DNSSEC relaxation toggle.
Create KB article describing DNSSEC / EDNS0 failure modes and recommended firewall rules for Private deployments.
